1.explanation:
• index.en-us.md & index.md: the core prop definitions (precision, step, defaultValue) and expected behavior.  
• precision.md: demo showing how precision prop is documented to work and where rounding logic lives.  
• step.md: demo of incremental behavior—how the + button should add step.  
• basic.md: generic usage to contrast default behavior without precision.  
• format.md: shows formatting logic applied to the displayed value.  
Together these reveal how step, precision and formatting interact and help locate where float rounding should be enforced to reproduce and then fix the Safari display bug.
1.bug_scenario: On Safari, when you render <NumberPicker defaultValue={4.02} step={0.01} /> (or with precision={2}) and click the “+” button, the control displays 4.029999999999999 instead of rounding to 4.03. The screenshot shows the NumberPicker’s input box (with its plus/minus buttons and background styling) showing the raw JS float error rather than applying the specified precision.
